title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 147, structure at infinity of M_{g,nu}). Grothendieck is axiomatising the combinatorial-analytic structure carried by the boundary of the Deligne-Mumford compactification, which is a divisor with normal crossings (in the orbifold sense) and possibly self-intersecting. The reading below of what D_d is comes from the indexing and the cartesian squares; the page does not state it.

Let X be the compactified moduli space (D_0 = X). Read D_d as the normalisation of the d-fold self-intersection locus. A point of D_d is a point x together with an unordered set of d local branches of the boundary through x.

The structure is given by:
(a) the family of analytic spaces (D_d).
(b) For each d, the S_d-torsor D_d^! -> D_d of orderings of those d branches. Hence I_d = {1,...,d} gives a twisted local system of finite sets over D_d.
(c) Put D_{d,d'} = D_d^! x^{S_d} P_{d'}(I_d), the space of choices of a d'-element subset of the d branches. This is a finite etale cover of D_d of degree binom(d,d').
  - Margin checks: D_{d,d} = D_{d,0} = D_d, and D_{d,1} is the d-sheeted cover attached to D_d^!.
  - The new datum is the 'target' map b: D_{d,d'} -> D_{d'}, which keeps only the chosen d' branches. For d' = 0 this is the map to X.
(d) Compatibility (175): the square with D^!_{d,d'} -> D^!_{d'} over b: D_{d,d'} -> D_{d'} is cartesian. Here D^!_{d,d'} is the S_{d'}-torsor of orderings of the tautological d'-sheeted cover of D_{d,d'}. In words: the local system of chosen branches is the pullback of the branch local system on D_{d'}.

Consequences on the page:
- The 'composable pairs' space D_{d,d',d''} = D^!_{d,d'} x^{S_{d'}} P_{d''}(I_{d'}) is determined by D_d^! alone (margin NB).
- (175) yields the cartesian square (176): D_{d,d',d''} = D_{d,d'} x_{D_{d'}} D_{d',d''}.

Together with the previous page (D_{d,*} = coprod D_{d,d'}, ordered by factorisability) and the next page (commutativity of the composition square (177); remark that the axioms make sense in any site), this describes the boundary as an internal category (or semi-simplicial-type object) in analytic spaces:
- objects: D_d;
- arrows: D_{d,d'};
- source maps: finite etale, with fibres the posets of subsets of a d-set;
- target maps: b;
- composition: via (176).

Purpose: recover the analytic 'structure at infinity' (the stratification together with its incidence and monodromy data) from these data. This prepares the link with 'revetements maximaux' and with the stable-graph combinatorics of the strata.
errors: Index inconsistency: (a) has d in N*, but (b) and (c) use d in N with D_0 = whole space (needed for D_{d,0} = D_d -> D_0). Minor.

The cartesian square (175) alone does not give the associativity / commutativity of composition. Grothendieck himself notes on the next page that (177) must be added or proved. The question raised on the previous page, whether D_{d,d''} -> D_d x D_{d''} is a monomorphism, is left open here.
D_{d,d'} is used before being formally defined from D_d^!. The definition comes only after (175).

ideas.what: Describe a normal-crossings boundary by the normalised d-fold strata D_d, the S_d-torsors of branch orderings, and the 'forget branches' maps D_{d,d'} -> D_{d'}, with D_{d,d'} = D_d^! x^{S_d} P_{d'}(I_d)
ideas.modern_name: Stratification/incidence category of a normal crossings divisor; monodromy of branches; closely related to the log structure (characteristic monoid N^d with S_d monodromy), the Artin fan, and the generalized cone complex / dual boundary complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971, normal crossings and orientation sheaves of branches); Kato and Fontaine-Illusie (log structures, 1980s); Abramovich-Caporaso-Payne (2015) and Abramovich-Chen-Marcus-Wise (Artin fans) for the cone-complex/category formulation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,nu} and its stratification by stable graphs, but this axiomatics is not there

ideas.what: Compatibility (175): the tautological branch torsor on D_{d,d'} is the pullback of D_{d'}^!; consequently the composable-pairs space D_{d,d',d''} is a fibre product (176)
ideas.modern_name: Internal category object in a site with finite etale source maps (a Boolean/simplicial-type category of strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the stratified-space and log-geometry literature

missed.claim: An axiomatic, site-independent definition of 'normal-crossings-type boundary structure' as an internal category whose source maps are finite etale torsor-twisted power-set posets and whose target maps satisfy the cartesian condition (175). It is intended to reconstruct the structure at infinity of M_{g,nu}, but is left with open questions: composition associativity (177), and whether arrows are determined by source and target.
missed.quote: la structure analytique peut se décrire par a) famille d'espaces analytiques (D_d) b) ... revêtement principal ... de groupe S_d ... c) des morphismes D_{d,d'} -> D_{d'} ... (175) ... cart
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates by decades the Artin-fan / generalized-cone-complex description of toroidal (DM) boundaries used in the tropical geometry of M_g (Abramovich-Caporaso-Payne). However, the idea of encoding strata with branch monodromy is now standard, so the novelty is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean early internal-category axiomatisation of the normal-crossings stratification of the boundary of M_{g,nu}, with S_d branch torsors. It is historically interesting as a precursor of log/tropical boundary combinatorics, but mathematically routine and largely subsumed by later theory.
transcription_corrections: The formula should read D_{d,d'} ≃ D_d^! x^{(S_d)_{D_d}} P_{d'}(I_d), with script P (subsets of cardinality d'), not double-struck D. Likewise D_{d,d',d''} = D^!_{d,d'} x^{(S_{d'})_{D_{d,d'}}} P_{d''}(I_{d'}).
The left margin begins '— avec D_{d,d} ≃ D_{d,0} ≃ D_d'. The second line reads approximately 'D_{d,1} est le rev. à d feuillets de D_d qui correspond à D_d^!'.
The struck-out line reads approximately 'D_{d,d',d''} =def D_{d,d'} x_{D_{d'}} D_{d',d''} -> D_d x D_{d''}', linked to the previous page's monomorphism question.
In (175) the bottom arrow is labelled b and the square is marked 'cart'.
